request:
Our school library wants a simple catalogue of its books. The librarian should be able to add a book with its title, its author and how many copies the library owns. Students should be able to see all the books, and look at one book to see how many copies are still on the shelf. A student borrows a book by giving their name, and returns it when they are done; a student can only return a book they actually borrowed. When every copy of a book is out, nobody else can borrow it until a copy comes back.

The client's answers to your questions:
Q: Can one student borrow more than one copy of the same book at the same time, and is there a limit on how many books one student can have out?
A: No preference: you decide.
Q: Does the librarian need to log in, and should students identify themselves only by typing their name, or do they need a login too? What if two students have the same name?
A: No, they just give their name.
Q: Should the librarian also be able to edit or remove a book, or change the number of copies after adding it, and is there a due date or history of past loans to track?
A: Not needed for now.

Where the client has no preference or did not answer, choose the simplest option and add nothing they did not ask for (no logins, PINs or extra required fields).
summary:
I wrote `app.py` and `tests/test_app.py`, and all 4 tests pass. Data is stored in a SQLite file, `library.db`, which is created when the app starts.

**Endpoints**
- `POST /books` adds a book with `title`, `author` and `copies`. It returns 201. Blank text or fewer than 1 copy is refused with 422.
- `GET /books` lists all books. Each one shows `copies` (owned) and `available` (still on the shelf).
- `GET /books/{id}` shows one book, including `available`. It returns 404 if the book doesn't exist.
- `POST /books/{id}/borrow` takes `{"student": "name"}` and returns 201. It returns 409 if every copy is out, or if that student already has this book.
- `POST /books/{id}/return` takes `{"student": "name"}`. It returns 409 if that student hasn't borrowed the book.

**Choices I made where you had no preference**
- A student can have only one copy of the same book at a time. I set no limit on how many different books they can have.
- Students are identified only by the name they type. Names are trimmed of spaces and can't be blank. Two students with the same name count as the same person.

I added nothing beyond what you asked for: no editing or removing books, no due dates, no loan history.
